statement: A report can be accurate and misleading at once when its evidence cites one file among many and never says how many were examined. A design partner running ten CI workflows concluded Cejel read only the first, because the certificate named one workflow and the other nine, which were all scored, left no trace. The disclosure must use the verb that is true for each criterion (B3 opens every workflow, so 'read'; A3 and B2 match workflow paths, so 'counted'), count a file the walk withheld as not read rather than read, and add nothing when read equals cited so the common case stays byte-identical. Rule: when evidence is a sample of what a metric consumed, state the consumed count beside the citation in the verb that is true of it.
